hints: Remember the naming order val-lys means valine provides the N-terminus ($\text{NH}_2$ end) and lysine provides the C-terminus ($\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ end).

Look up the two R groups, isopropyl $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}$ for valine and 4-aminobutyl $(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$ for lysine, and join the two units by removing water to leave $\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{N}(\text{H})$ displayed.
walkthrough:
Place the two amino acids in the correct order**
Think of a dipeptide as written left to right from N to C. So val-lys starts with valine with its free $\text{NH}_2$ on the left, and ends with lysine with its free $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ on the right. The link in the middle is formed when the $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ of valine reacts with the $\text{NH}_2$ on the alpha carbon of lysine, losing $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Add the correct side chains and display the link**
Valine has the branched side chain $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CH-}$ attached to its alpha carbon, so the left unit is $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH(NH}_2\text{)-}$. Lysine has the basic side chain $\text{-(CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$ attached to its alpha carbon, so the right unit is $\text{-NHCH((CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2\text{)CO}_2\text{H}$. In the centre draw every bond of the amide link out fully as $\text{C(=O)-N(H)-}$, not just as $\text{CONH}$.

Final answer: $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH(NH}_2\text{)C(=O)NHCH((CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2\text{)CO}_2\text{H}$
Peptide bond $\text{-C(=O)-NH-}$ shown displayed with C=O and N-H bonds drawn out. Correct valine isopropyl side chain on left alpha carbon and lysine $(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_2$ side chain on right alpha carbon.

hints: Recall that at pH equal to the isoelectric point the species has zero net charge and will not migrate in an electric field.
Compare the buffer pH of 6.0 with the isoelectric point of lysine, 9.8, to decide whether lysine and any lysine containing peptide will be protonated or deprotonated.
Remember that positively charged species are attracted toward the negative electrode (cathode) on the right of the diagram.
Consider what the net charge will be on lysine and on val-lys at pH 6.0 by counting $\text{NH}_3^+$ and $\text{CO}_2^-$ groups.
For two ions with the same charge, think about how relative molecular mass, $M_r$, affects how far they move through the paper or gel.
walkthrough:
Work out the charge on valine at pH 6.0**
Picture a zwitterion as $\text{RCH(NH}_3^+\text{)(CO}_2^-\text{)}$ with one plus and one minus cancelling to zero. The pH where this happens is the isoelectric point. Here buffer pH 6.0 exactly equals the pI of valine, 6.0, so valine is neutral overall and feels no pull from either electrode. It stays where you spotted it, on the cross.

Work out the charge on lysine and val-lys at pH 6.0**
Lysine has an extra basic $\text{NH}_2$ in its side chain, which is why its pI is high at 9.8. At the much more acidic pH of 6.0 there is excess $\text{H}^+$, so the side chain is protonated to $\text{(CH}_2)_4\text{NH}_3^+$. Counting groups: $\text{CO}_2^-$ gives -1, alpha $\text{NH}_3^+$ gives +1, side $\text{NH}_3^+$ gives +1, net +1. The dipeptide val-lys still contains that same lysine side chain plus one $\text{NH}_3^+$ at the N-terminus and one $\text{CO}_2^-$ at the C-terminus, so it is also net +1.

Decide the direction of movement**
Positive ions migrate toward the negative pole. That is the electrode labelled minus on the right hand side of the paper. So both lysine and val-lys move to the right of the origin, while valine stays in the centre.

Separate lysine from val-lys by size**
Both moving species carry the same +1 charge, so charge alone cannot separate them. A smaller ion slips through the support medium more easily and travels further in the same time. Lysine, $M_r$ about 146, is much lighter than val-lys, $M_r$ about 245 ($117 + 146 - 18$ for loss of water). Therefore lysine moves furthest toward the negative end, and val-lys moves a shorter distance, sitting between valine and lysine.

Draw and label the final pattern**
Mark three clear spots on the centre line: label val on the X, label val-lys a short distance to the right of X, label lys a longer distance to the right of X, all still well away from the electrodes. Your written explanation must state the neutral versus +1 charge argument and the $M_r$ argument to link position to theory.

Final answer: Diagram: valine remains on the cross (origin); val-lys and lysine both move to the right toward the negative pole, with lysine furthest to the right and val-lys between valine and lysine.
Valine at pH 6.0 = pI is a neutral zwitterion so does not move. Lysine and val-lys at pH 6.0 < pI are protonated with +1 net charge so move toward the negative pole. Lysine has lower $M_r$ than val-lys with the same +1 charge so moves furthest.
